The City of Buckeye executed a development agreement with AZLCO Buckeye, LLC (Ordinance No. 08-24, adopted unanimously 2024-08-06). It reimburses the developer for six enumerated regional infrastructure components it builds and dedicates to the city — two public-safety sites, temporary and permanent public-safety facilities, $15M toward the Johnson Road interchange, and oversized regional water infrastructure — funded by 20% of the tax revenue the project itself generates, beginning only after the city has received $60M cumulatively and terminating 20 years from the effective date. It is capped at "the lesser of" the developer's verified costs or $50,000,000, so it cannot exceed what the developer actually spent; it is cost recovery for public infrastructure rather than an incentive, abatement or credit, and is therefore not recorded as a subsidy. Nothing has been paid to date. Buckeye's economic-development director has projected "more than 360 jobs at full build out" — an end-state across as many as 40 separate future data centers, none yet leased, permitted or built, and so not recorded as a permanent-jobs figure for this site. properties.name: AWS Costas Property Campus (Ridgeland)
properties.note: RESOLVES last wave's hold with independent primary-tier evidence that Canton and Ridgeland are genuinely two distinct AWS campuses, not a single project under two names. Mississippi Free Press (2026-08-19), reporting Madison County's denial of AWS's tax-valuation appeal, states directly: 'The county has entered into two fee-in-lieu-of-taxes agreements with the tech giant for its data center campuses in Canton and Ridgeland' -- i.e., Madison County's own tax/incentive administration treats these as two separate FILOT agreements, not one. Magnolia Tribune (2024-07-24, re-fetched this run) gives the physical distinction: the Madison County Mega Site is '927 acres ... located off Highway 22 and Nissan Parkway in Canton,' while the Costas Property is 'an additional 786 acres in Ridgeland ... located along the southern tip of Madison County near Tougaloo College, on the corner of Highland Colony Parkway and West County Line Road' -- roughly 20 miles apart. Both sites are within Madison County (Ridgeland is not a separate county), so the live aggregate record's id/framing as 'Madison County' is not wrong on that count, but it does combine two separately-incentivized campuses. Coordinates are the OSM-tagged traffic-signal node at the actual Highland Colony Parkway / West County Line Road intersection (confirmed via Overpass API query against current OpenStreetMap way data, not an estimate), not a confirmed parcel boundary -- precision 'approximate'. Deliberately omitted: capacityMw, investmentUsd, and jobs, because every figure found for this project (the $10B investment, the combined MW target, job counts) is stated for the two-site project as a whole; no source fetched this run apportions any of these by site, and apportioning by acreage share would be a fabricated estimate, not a sourced fact. See the companion refresh finding on aws-project-atlas-madison-county-ms recommending it be re-scoped to the Canton site alone.

Amazon's total Mississippi statewide commitment expanded to $25B including subsequent Warren County ($3B) and Hinds County ($1B) announcements. Coordinates are approximate Canton-area centroid. Veolia water partnership claim removed: About Amazon source names Arable (not Veolia) as water replenishment partner; recycled wastewater target of 83M gallons/year by 2027 is confirmed. NARROWED TO CANTON 2026-09-10 (maintainer adjudication): this record previously combined two campuses. Madison County's own tax administration treats them as separate — it 'has entered into two fee-in-lieu-of-taxes agreements with the tech giant for its data center campuses in Canton and Ridgeland' (Mississippi Free Press, 2026-08-19) — and Magnolia Tribune (2024-07-24) gives the physical split: the Madison County Mega Site is '927 acres ... located off Highway 22 and Nissan Parkway in Canton', while the Costas Property is 'an additional 786 acres in Ridgeland'. The Ridgeland campus is therefore now tracked separately as aws-costas-ridgeland-ms, and landAcres here was reduced from the combined 1,700 to Canton's 927 so the two records do not double-count acreage. ⚠️ capacityMw, investmentUsd and jobs on this record remain PROGRAM-LEVEL figures from the original Project Atlas announcement covering BOTH Madison County campuses; they are deliberately left in place here rather than split, because no source apportions them per campus. Do NOT sum them with aws-costas-ridgeland-ms, which carries no capacity, investment or jobs figures for exactly this reason. location.precision was also corrected from 'exact' to 'approximate': this record's own notes already stated the coordinate is a Canton-area centroid, so the 'exact' claim was wrong. CORRECTION: this record aggregates two campuses that Madison County's own tax/incentive administration treats as legally and financially separate -- the Madison County Mega Site (927 acres, off Highway 22 and Nissan Parkway, Canton) and the Costas Property (786 acres, Highland Colony Parkway / West County Line Road, Ridgeland) -- confirmed by a 2026-08-19 Mississippi Free Press report on Madison County's denial of AWS's Canton tax-valuation appeal: the county 'has entered into two fee-in-lieu-of-taxes agreements with the tech giant for its data center campuses in Canton and Ridgeland.' Recommend re-scoping this record to the Canton (Madison County Mega Site) campus alone -- its location.lat/lon (32.6121, -90.039) and 'exact' precision already read as Canton-specific, closer to Canton than to Ridgeland -- and using the companion new-facility record aws-costas-ridgeland-ms (786 acres, Highland Colony Pkwy/West County Line Rd intersection) for Ridgeland. Do NOT attempt to apportion this record's combined capacityMw (1000 MW planned), investmentUsd ($10B), or jobs (7,000/1,000) by site -- no source fetched in this run or last wave's states a per-site breakdown of those figures; apportioning by acreage share (54%/46%) would be a fabricated estimate. Note also that Ridgeland is itself within Madison County, so the aggregate's 'Madison County' framing is not geographically wrong, only combined.

WKTV: "Turin Hoefler Avenue LLC submitted a revised application" to the NYSDEC "Brownfield Cleanup Program" in January 2026 for "Site C," a "7.837-acre parcel," with a "250,000-square-foot AI data center" as the intended post-remediation use, at "14 Hoefler Ave., Ilion, NY"; the site has "widespread contamination in the soil, especially with heavy metals like arsenic, lead, and copper at levels above state cleanup standards for commercial use" and "15 vacant industrial buildings dating to the early 1900s," and the developer describes it as a "fossil-fuel-free, 100% electric site." capacityMw.planned = 200 comes from the Rockefeller Institute of Government's tracker entry for the project ("200 MW"), not from WKTV, which states no MW figure. COUNTY DISCREPANCY, recorded honestly: WKTV's article says Oneida County; the Rockefeller Institute says "Village of Ilion, Herkimer County." Ilion is in Herkimer County, so Herkimer is recorded and the WKTV attribution is treated as an error. landAcres = 7.837 is the Brownfield Site C parcel only; trade press describes a larger ~32-acre overall plant site and two 250,000 sq ft buildings, neither of which was verified against a fetched source, so neither is recorded. jobs.permanent is deliberately omitted: the source says only that the project "aims to exceed the 274 positions lost when Remington closed," which is an aspiration, not a count. Confirmed absences (2026-09-09): no investment figure, no water/cooling detail, no utility, and no IDA or PILOT agreement stated in either fetched source. Because the site is fossil-fuel-free and 100% electric per the developer, no on-site generation is recorded.

Capacity: 75 MW disclosed operating load at opening vs. 150 MW max design load (city FAQ) -- both real, tracked field carries the larger design figure. Investment: ~$1.3B total project cost (multi-source) vs. $901.3M JobsOhio incentive-scoped committed investment -- tracked field carries the total-project figure. 120 permanent jobs / >$14M annual payroll disclosed (WYSO); a separate JobsOhio incentive filing cites 20 committed data-infrastructure jobs (narrower, incentive-scoped count). Incentives: ~$95M city enterprise-zone abatement over 15 years; $32M+ state 10-year 50% Ohio Tax Credit Authority credit (Oct 2025) to The Constant Company. Community context: Springfield passed a 6-month moratorium on new data centers and a citizen petition to ban them was launched; Clark County (Jul 2026) restricted data centers to I-2 heavy-industrial zoning, but the county's own zoning administrator noted no I-2 parcels currently exist in county jurisdiction, and Springfield Township (where Prime Ohio sits) zones separately from the county -- this rule change may not directly bind this site.

TWO SITES are named in the DOE release: one at the East Tennessee Technology Park and one on land adjacent to Oak Ridge National Laboratory. This is recorded as a single record with representative_multi_site precision, geocoded to the East Tennessee Technology Park, because DOE names two sites but publishes no design, footprint, or capacity for either; splitting it would duplicate a record with no site-specific facts. ORNL itself geocodes to 35.9301332, -84.3119307. CONFIRMED ABSENCES as of 2026-09-09: no lessee has been selected, no capacity, investment, footprint or timeline is stated, and applicants — not DOE — are responsible for securing utility interconnection agreements and all permitting. The operator field records DOE as the landowner and solicitor, NOT as the eventual data-center operator, which is unknown. Oak Ridge is one of four federal sites DOE identified for AI infrastructure. Distinct from the existing Kairos Power Hermes 2 record, which is a separate NRC-licensed reactor project at Oak Ridge.

properties.name: Project Tembo
properties.power: On-site natural gas (Tallgrass Cheyenne Power Hub)
properties.note: Switchgrass Industrial Park, Hwy 85 south of Cheyenne, Laramie County - geographically distinct from Meta (Project Cosmo) and Microsoft's Cheyenne campuses. 716-acre campus. Originally announced at 1.8GW as 'Project Jade' with an undisclosed hyperscale client (Crusoe Energy as builder); Crusoe exited June 2026. On 2026-07-08, Google was publicly revealed as owner/operator via subsidiary Jupiter Star Holdings, and the project was renamed 'Project Tembo'; capacity confirmed at 2.7GW with an ultimate ceiling of up to 10GW. The Cheyenne Power Hub on-site natural-gas plant supplies power (Tallgrass Energy; Black Hills Energy co-invested). ~$50B total project figure remains a projection. Completion targeted 2031.
